answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and lists its stock in an append-only shale ledger. Every unit moves on one thread from stock to a key-signed delivery receipt, used once. Auditors recount stock against delivered plus held units; a reused or broken thread burns the bond. The zenith ceiling caps each identity at 50 units, so one identity cannot carry many stocks. A fake pays 70 plus 50 units at 4 credits, 270 total; the kth fake pays 270, and 1,000 fakes cost 270,000. Rented stock fails on recount, while an honest identity pays 270 once and keeps its bond.
